name: door-strength-levelling-v1
description: READ THIS BEFORE READING THE ARM, BECAUSE THIS IS NOT THE WELD ARM. Wayfinder ticket 10 asked for an overlay that BREAKS THE WELD between the visit door and the host's suit. NO OVERLAY CAN EXPRESS THAT. The weld is `serviceIdOf` in packages/engine/src/query.ts reading `linkedSuit` off workers.json, and the knob registry (packages/data/src/knobs.ts) exposes exactly four per-door leaves: draw.see, draw.keep, sow.amount and deliver.handToBarn. There is no knob for a door's `action`, none for `linkedSuit`, none for the Dairy door's build discount or waiver, and none for the Wheat door's relaxedMin. Every reading of 'break the weld' (visitor chooses the action / one generic action for all doors / the action shuffled onto suits at setup) is an ENGINE change of roughly ten to twenty lines, not a tuning change, so building it as an overlay would have been a proxy answering a different question. This arm is the NARROWER FAITHFUL EXPERIMENT instead. THE HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST is the middle link of T1's causal chain: visitors go where the useful action is, therefore the door's action decides its traffic. If that link holds, door traffic must be ELASTIC to door strength, and levelling the strengths must level the traffic. So: the top-traffic door is weakened and the two weakest REACHABLE doors are strengthened. Draw (Orchard, 36% of rival uses) goes from see 3 keep 3 to see 2 keep 2, which is exactly the 'plain Draw 2' the workers.json note says the design intends and the data does not currently ship; it stays card-POSITIVE, so the self-cancellation law is not broken and the door is not made worthless. Sow (Apiary, 12%) goes from 1 to 2. Deliver (Vegetable, 18%) goes from handToBarn 1 to 2. THE TWO UNREACHABLE DOORS ARE THE INTERNAL CONTROLS: Build (Dairy, 24%) and Harvest (Wheat, 10%) are untouched, so if the three moved doors trade share while those two hold their ground, elasticity is confirmed AND localised. WHAT TO READ: assertion 7's detail line, which is the only place the five-way door split is printed, so this arm needs `--watchlist --overlay=` as well as `--sweep=` (the sweep table prints assertion 7's value alone, which is the draw door only). Then the SUITS table, because the point of the exercise is the 37.3-point win-rate spread. WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT SHOW: whether decoupling the action from the suit evens out traffic BY SUIT. That is true by construction under any weld-break and needs no arm; the open question a real weld-break would answer is whether evening it out by suit closes the win-rate spread, and only an engine change can ask it. WHAT ELSE LIMITS THE CLAIM: the Apiary door in this engine runs 'Sow the top card of any deck', while the printed A3 says 'Draw 2, then you may GROW one of your buildings'. Change 16 never landed in code (Dean, 2026-09-02: label it, do not fix it). The sow lever below therefore moves a door the physical game does not have, and every Apiary figure it produces is measured-on-the-wrong-door.
